messages:
alex: Ran a perfetto capture on the quantize-prefetch change, attaching the heatmap link. 95th pctl latency jumps correlate with repeated L2 eviction waves.
mira: can you paste the perfetto range/trace id? quick skim pls
alex: https://perfetto.dev/trace/#trace_id=abcd1234 (range pinned 00:01:20-00:02:05)
chen: looking now. Do you see the kernel switch thrash or memory stalls?
alex: timeline shows frequent memcpy spikes, but kernel timelines indicate the same kernel is being reselected often after prefetch finishes.
devon: that sounds like the new prefetch handoff heuristic is stomping KV cache hot paths. any before/after captures?
alex: yes — before (1745544000) vs after (1745559100). I diffed slices: before had steady kernel A mainline; after we see 3x more short kernel B invocations around the same token window.
mira: can you paste the snippet of the flame summary? small paste helps
alex: ```
# perfetto flame summary (excerpt)
00:01:25 kernel_A  48.2%
00:01:25 kernel_B  22.1%  <-- new
00:01:25 memcpy     18.0%  <-- spike
00:01:25 scheduler  11.7%
```
chen: memcpy spike looks like KV cache affinity bounce. Are we invalidating prefixes on prefetch completion?
devon: code change was here: runtime/scheduler/prefetch_handoff.cc: changed policy from hold-to-complete -> eager-swap after N ms. Could cause early release of KV pages.
alex: confirmed — the eager-swap path triggers a kernel probe that forces immediate variant probe, which yields small runs of kernel_B while kernel_A warms back up.
mira: can we reproduce on smaller sequence locally? I can run nsys-ish perfetto with small input and toggles
alex: repro steps (local):
1) checkout 5d2b7c2 (before) and run perfetto trace
2) checkout a8c9f1e (after) and run same test harness: ./tools/run_infer --batch 4 --seq 1024 --profile
3) compare heatmaps -> look at L2 eviction bands around tokens 300-500
devon: I ran the local test. After change, tail latency variance up ~27% and observed eviction waves when two concurrent requests cross the same KV stripe.
perf-bot: detected pattern match: "kv-eviction-wave" previously seen in 1724301234-prefetch-stall-heuristics. Recommending bisect.
alex: I started a git bisect between 5d2b7c2..a8c9f1e to isolate the exact commit that introduced the handoff tweak.
mira: progress update?
alex: bisect landed on commit ff7e2a1: small logic change in prefetch_handoff.cc that switches swap threshold to 0.02s from 0.2s.
chen: that 10x lower threshold explains aggressive swaps. We should revert or make it dynamic based on KV cache occupancy.
devon: immediate revert candidate: rollback ff7e2a1 in canary to validate latency improvement.
alex: FYI I ran quick canary with revert patch (revert-ff7e2a1) on staging: 95th pctl went back to baseline, memcpy spikes disappeared in perfetto.
mira: nice. what's the rollout plan? patch + test + telemetry?
alex: propose revert in a small PR, add a feature-flag gated A/B and add a telemetry counter for "prefetch_eager_swap" and KV eviction rate. I'll attach the perfetto compare screenshots to the PR.
chen: also add an integration test that exercises concurrent small-window requests to catch eviction waves in CI perf runs.
devon: thanks — I'll raise the PR and request a quick ops deploy to canary, and we'll monitor telemetry for 24h before wider rollout.
alex: sounds good. summary: root cause = threshold change in prefetch handoff -> aggressive swap -> kernel reselection thrash -> memcpy / L2 eviction waves -> latency spikes. Revert validated in staging.
mira: :thumbsup: please ping when PR is up
alex: will do. attaching perfetto ranges and the bisect commit id in the PR.
